title: TA9-09364
frame:
Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX is a citizen of Colombia. She claims for refugee protection pursuant to Sections 96, 97(1)(a) and 97(1)(b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

The claimant alleges she was actively involved in Colombian politics. Her problems with the Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionaries de Colombia (FARC) guerrillas began in 1987 while she was working as a XXXXX XXXXX. The FARC demanded that she XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX She told them that she had no authority to help them in that area. In 1988, the FARC demanded that XXXXX XXXXX, including her, resign from their positions. When the FARC began killing XXXXX XXXXX who failed to meet their demands, the claimant ended working as a City Councillor in 1989.

In 1993, the FARC confiscated the claimant's XXXXX XXXXX with its contents. Subsequently, in 1995, when she became a XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, she began receiving threatening letters from the FARC demanding that she resign from her position or die. In 1997, her home in XXXXX XXXXX was bombed and, six months later, her colleague, XXXXX XXXXX, was murdered by the FARC. As a result of her colleague's murder, she resigned from her position in the XXXXX XXXXX and permanently located in Bogota. She maintained her XXXXX XXXXX.

In 1999, after the Colombian government reached an agreement to create a demilitarized zone for the FARC, she returned to XXXXX XXXXX. In 2001, the claimant, accompanied with XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, filed a denunciation against the FARC for continued threats and extortion demands. In XXXXX 2002, she filed a denunciation against the FARC with the Public Prosecutor's office in Bogota for threats made against her when her tenant, backed by the FARC, refused to vacate her house in XXXXX XXXXX.

The determinative issues in this case are subjective and whether, at this time, her fear is objectively well-founded. Based on the evidence adduced, the panel does not find that the claimant has a subjective fear of persecution in Colombia, as well as her fear is not objectively well-founded.

With regard to credibility, the panel is aware that testimony given under oath is presumed to be true, unless there is a valid reason to doubt its truthfulness.1 The panel is also aware that the real test of the truth of a story of a witness is that it be in harmony with the preponderance of probabilities which a practical and informed person would readily recognise as reasonable in that place and in those conditions.2 Furthermore, the panel cannot be satisfied that, "the evidence is credible or trustworthy unless satisfied that it is probably so, not just possibly so".3

In reviewing the evidence, the panel considered the claimant's oral and written evidence, her counsel's written submissions and all of the documentary evidence entered as exhibits. Based on the totality of the evidence adduced, the panel finds that the claimant lacked subjective fear which is not objectively well-founded.

In this case, the claimant indicated that she fears the FARC guerrilla group in Colombia. She indicated that her problems with the FARC began in 1987 but she did not leave Colombia until 2003. She testified that in 2002 she applied for refugee protection at the Canadian Embassy in Bogota. When her application for refugee protection was refused, she decided to flee to Italy in XXXXX 2003. She lived in Italy on a temporary status until XXXXX 2007 and thereafter she decided to return to Colombia, the country where she feared persecution at the hands of the FARC. She indicated that she did not apply for asylum in Italy because she intended to return to Colombia expecting the peace talks between the FARC and the Colombian Government to succeed.

Her expectations to return to Colombia after peace talks between the Government of Colombia and the FARC succeeded are not reasonable since peace talks between the two parties had collapsed in XXXXX of 2002,4 before she left to go to Italy. The panel finds that the claimant's long stay in Italy, without making an attempt to file for asylum, and her return to Colombia is indicative of lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC.

The claimant testified that she lived in Colombia for six to seven months before returning to Italy. Her six to seven months' stay in Colombia is indicative of lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC. Once she returned to Italy, she failed to make an asylum claim in that country. Her failure to make an asylum claim during her second visit to Italy is another example of lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia. Her return to Colombia where she feared the FARC for the second time also indicates that she lacked subjective fear of persecution in that country.

After she returned to Colombia from Italy, threats from the FARC continued and as a result she decided to go to Mexico in XXXXX of 2008. In Mexico, she lived with her daughter until XXXXX, 2008 before returning to Colombia. She indicated that she did not file for asylum in Mexico because she had no plans to do so since she was only visiting her daughter. Since she was allegedly threatened by the FARC in Colombia, her failure to seek asylum in Mexico, a country signatory to refugee Convention, indicates that she lacked subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia. Her reason for returning to obtain USA visas from the USA embassy in Colombia is not reasonable since she could have obtained those visas at the USA embassy in Mexico. Her return to Colombia on XXXXX 2008 is another example of lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia.

After receiving the USA visas, she returned to Mexico in XXXXX 2009. Once again she made no attempt to regularize her status in Mexico. Her actions indicate her lack of subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia. From Mexico she went to Las Vegas and then to Canada. She indicated that she did not plan to apply for asylum in the USA because she wanted to join her brother in Canada.

The claimant's brother is a resident of Canada since 2003. He was a successful refugee applicant. The claimant had knowledge about the refugee protection in Canada since she had applied for refugee protection at the Canadian embassy in Bogota in 2002. Although her brother had status in Canada since 2003, and, given that she was in contact with him since he left Colombia, the claimant made no effort to come to Canada to regularize her status earlier. She chose to go to Italy and Mexico instead. Her actions indicate lack of subjective fear of persecution from the FARC in Colombia.

Based on the evidence adduced, the claimant's behaviour and her actions indicate that she lacked subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia. The panel is not persuaded to believe that she feared the FARC after she resigned from her XXXXX XXXXX position in 1997.

Moreover, the claimant testified that she was continuously threatened by the FARC, after she resigned from her position as a member of XXXXX XXXXX She also indicated that on one occasion she was personally contacted by the commander of the FARC from XXXXX XXXXX. At the hearing she did not provide any documentary evidence, such as a police report or an affidavit, to indicate that she was threatened by the FARC after her resignation from the XXXXX XXXXX in 1997. She did not provide media articles and/or affidavits either from her daughter in Colombia or from other colleagues and friends to corroborate that she was threatened by the FARC after she left her XXXXX XXXXX position. Also she did not provide persuasive reasons for failing to provide such documents to help the panel in its decision. The onus is on her to establish her claim particularly when she was instructed in question 31 to provide documentary evidence to establish her claim.

Her failure to provide the aforementioned documentary evidence raises a serious doubt in the panel's mind as to whether the FARC had any further interest to harm the claimant when she resigned from the XXXXX XXXXX. The panel therefore does not believe that the claimant was threatened by the FARC after she resigned.

Also the FARC demanded that she resign from her position at the XXXXX XXXXX which she did. As a result, the panel is not persuaded to believe that the FARC had any interest to harm her after she complied with their demands. The panel finds that the claimant has fabricated her story about threats from the FARC after 1997 to bolster her refugee claim.

Based on the evidence adduced, the panel does not believe that the FARC threatened the claimant after she resigned from her position at the XXXXX XXXXX in 1997 because they had no interest to do so. As a result, the panel does not find that the claimant has an objectively well-founded fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC in Colombia.

Professor Hathaway has said that it is appropriate to inquire into the circumstances of any protracted postponement of a refugee claim as a means of evaluating the sincerity of the claimant's need for protection.5

In Leon, the claimant waited over five years to make a claim. Justice Muldoon of the Federal Court commented: It is incredible that he [the claimant] would believe that he could not make a refugee claim because he was an illegal ........ That is incredible. That he would wait for 5 years in that belief, if that belief were true, is even more incredible.6

Based on the totality of the evidence adduced, and because the claimant lacked subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC, and since her fear is not objectively well-founded, the panel finds that there is less than a mere possibility that she would be persecuted by the FARC should she return to Colombia.

The panel's credibility findings also apply to the claimant's assertion that she faces a risk to his life or of being subjected to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment in Colombia. Since the claimant lacks subjective fear of persecution at the hands of the FARC, and her fear is not objectively well-founded, the panel finds that the claimant does not face a risk to her life or to being subjected to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment or to a danger of being tortured, should she return to Colombia.

Also, the panel has reviewed all of the documentation entered as exhibits in this case. Based on the documentary evidence, there is no persuasive evidence to indicate that, at this time, the claimant will be subjected to any other risk, other than the risk of general violence which all citizens in Colombia are subjected to.
Therefore, the panel finds that the claimant is not a Convention refugee, nor she is a person in need of protection pursuant to sections 97(1)(a) and 97(1)(b) of the IRPA.

Accordingly, the Refugee Protection Division rejects the claim of XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX for refugee protection. (signed) 'S. Alidina' S.
